From d8c2f5c586cff21448c510ea40dc50b3e412294f Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Willy Tarreau <w@1wt.eu>
Date: Fri, 12 Apr 2024 12:01:31 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] BUG/MEDIUM: peers/trace: fix crash when listing event types

Sending "trace peers event" on the CLI crashes because the event list
in the peers is not finished. This was introduced in 2.4 by commit
d865935f32 ("MINOR: peers: Add traces to peer_treat_updatemsg().")
so this must be backported to 2.4.

diff --git a/src/peers.c b/src/peers.c
index 1182c2117..1e9a690f3 100644
--- a/src/peers.c
+++ b/src/peers.c
@@ -334,6 +334,7 @@ static const struct trace_event peers_trace_events[] = {
 	{ .mask = PEERS_EV_SESSREL,    .name = "sessrl",       .desc = "peer session releasing" },
 #define PEERS_EV_PROTOERR        (1 << 6)
 	{ .mask = PEERS_EV_PROTOERR,   .name = "protoerr",     .desc = "protocol error" },
+	{ }
 };
 
 static const struct name_desc peers_trace_lockon_args[4] = {
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `src/peers.c`**
   - A new entry `{ }` was added to the end of the `peers_trace_events` array. This entry serves as a terminator for the list of event types, ensuring that the array is properly concluded.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modification in `src/peers.c` addresses a bug that caused a crash when executing the command "trace peers event" in the CLI. The crash occurred because the event list was not properly terminated, which was a regression introduced in a previous commit. By adding the terminator entry to the event list, the patch ensures that the event types are correctly recognized and processed, thus preventing the crash. This fix is intended to be backported to version 2.4 of the software.

Here is the commit message:
BUG/MEDIUM: peers/trace: fix crash when listing event types

Sending "trace peers event" on the CLI crashes because the event list
in the peers is not finished. This was introduced in 2.4 by commit
d865935f32 ("MINOR: peers: Add traces to peer_treat_updatemsg().")
so this must be backported to 2.4.

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the absence of a terminator entry in the `peers_trace_events` array, which led to an incomplete event list. This resulted in a crash when the "trace peers event" command was executed, as the system attempted to access an undefined portion of the array.

Here is the patch:
 #define PEERS_EV_PROTOERR        (1 << 6)
 	{ .mask = PEERS_EV_PROTOERR,   .name = "protoerr",     .desc = "protocol error" },
+	{ }
 };

Adding a terminator entry to the `peers_trace_events` array ensures that the system recognizes the end of the event list, preventing it from accessing undefined memory and thus avoiding the crash when executing the "trace peers event" command.
